Codex review: blocked before merge. _Reviewed September 5, 2026, 8:58 AM ET / 12:58 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Give each agent its own generated-skill directory, migrate existing Workshop state, and anchor background learning to the completed conversation turn. > [!WARNING] > **SQLite table change** > > This PR modifies persisted SQLite tables in `src/skills/workshop/store-sqlite-schema.ts`, `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`. Prefer a design that avoids changing persisted SQLite tables. If the change is necessary, verify migration and upgrade compatibility against an existing database before merge. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** Keep open: the agent-owned Workshop remains distinct from current main and the latest release. Prior actionable findings are addressed, and the recorded migration decisions should not be reopened as new blockers. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `c19749909bf73109fe6f532705378101c8d8ff2e` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A coherent ownership refactor with substantial regression coverage and retained runtime evidence; compatibility tradeoffs are explicitly accepted. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (linked_artifact): Retained real Doctor runs demonstrate recovery with a competing SQLite writer, and supplied CLI/Gateway observations cover grouped audit and agent isolation; matching recovery and audit sources remain unchanged. Historical learning proof is not relabeled as a current-head run, and remote artifacts could not be reopened. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (linked_artifact): Retained real Doctor runs demonstrate recovery with a competing SQLite writer, and supplied CLI/Gateway observations cover grouped audit and agent isolation; matching recovery and audit sources remain unchanged. Historical learning proof is not relabeled as a current-head run, and remote artifacts could not be reopened. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 13 items | Pinned introduction and continuity: The complete local base-to-head comparison contains 202 introduced paths. Tree comparison confirms 193 are unchanged since the previous reviewed head, including recovery, audit, discovery, and Codex finalization. The supplied test merge is stale and was not used to infer removal of main-branch behavior.
Still necessary on current main: Current main still resolves proposal targets under the session workspace's skills directory and retains state schema 15.
Latest release behavior: The supplied v2026.9.1 release revision also resolves generated targets under workspace/skills; it does not provide this PR's per-agent directory ownership. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Skill Workshop turns chat requests and completed agent work into reviewed skill proposals. Its storage, approval, recovery, and discovery paths determine which generated instructions later agent runs receive. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Chat and CLI requests] --> B[Agent-scoped proposals] C[Completed agent turns] --> B B --> D[Approval and security scan] D --> E[Agent Workshop files] F[Legacy skills and state] --> G[Doctor migration] G --> B G --> E E --> H[Skill discovery for later turns] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The accepted upgrade retires workspace symlink-target writes and automatic restore pointers with ambiguous ownership; some operators will need the documented manual recovery path. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Reviewer-side gaps remain in linked artifact access, fs-safe implementation inspection, and comparison of intervening changes since the historical live-learning run. - [ ] **Review config compatibility** - Confirm compatibility and upgrade impact for the changed config or default surface before merge. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.
Agent review details ### Security None. ### PR surface PR surface statistics unavailable: the file list is incomplete. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus test growth** | Production net +1,390 lines; tests/support net +5,262 lines | Excluding documentation and generated baselines, growth supports agent ownership and migration recovery; moved code cancels in the net. | | **Upgrade contract** | Schema 15→16; 2 proposal columns removed; 1 history table rekeyed; 1 setting retired | These accepted changes affect existing installations and their recovery behavior. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `database schema: src/skills/workshop/store-sqlite-schema.ts`, `database schema: src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`, `migration/backfill/repair: config/assertion-safety-baseline.txt`, `migration/backfill/repair: src/state/openclaw-state-db-schema-repair.ts`, `migration/backfill/repair: src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts`, `serialized state: src/skills/workshop/skills-root.ts`, and 4 more. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Retain the accepted upgrade contract (recommended)** Proceed under the recorded migration decision while preserving stale-proposal diagnostics, retained files, and documented manual backup recovery. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain one agent-owned proposal, apply, and recovery pipeline with the accepted migration safeguards; keep the weekly review-turn redesign in its separate follow-up. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Not applicable to the overall feature proposal; its component repairs have recorded before/after CLI evidence, but this read-only review did not execute them. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes: agent-owned storage fixes ownership at its producer while reusing the existing proposal service and discovery machinery; workspace-only adjustments or profile-owned libraries would not provide the same boundary. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning high; reviewed against [177a1e3b054e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/177a1e3b054e75a4a24af75a75a09519cf8cf5dd). ### Labels Label justifications: - `P2`: This is a useful, actively maintained ownership improvement without an established urgent production outage. - `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`: Schema migration and setting retirement intentionally change existing Workshop workflows and automatic recovery eligibility. - `rating: 🐚 platinum hermit`: Overall readiness is 🐚 platinum hermit; proof is 🦞 diamond lobster and patch quality is 🐚 platinum hermit. - `status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`: ClawSweeper has no concrete contributor-facing blocker left for this PR. Thanks @obviyus!

Landed as [a4514a0](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/a4514a0aff9de7bd299f70d821398df606df1a4f).

**Proof:** The retained rebuilt CLI preserves current proposals while another connection holds the SQLite write lock. All 156 integration tests passed on tree `459b8fc3d0a51ec0461a6e8079f564786755bd4e`. Earlier source-bound proof covers interrupted-write recovery, agent isolation, grouped-skill audit, and live-provider learning. These observations retain their original build identities; the owning Workshop code is unchanged. The fresh exact-head local ClawSweeper review passed at Platinum with no findings.

- **Bug:** Workspace-derived ownership and competing write/recovery paths made background learning unreliable.
- **Fix:** Each agent has one writable Workshop collection. Review uses the completed turn, and Doctor recovers interrupted writes before relocating legacy skills.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Changing workspaces could change skill ownership | One stable Workshop home per agent |
| Current proposals could make no-op Doctor contend for a write lock | Doctor skips ineligible legacy recovery and preserves the proposal |
| Interrupted writes could become unreadable during relocation | Recovery and relocation share one owner; blocked drafts remain inspectable |

[Reviewed source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c19749909bf73109fe6f532705378101c8d8ff2e). [Retained integrated CLI proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_cb30a7036544).

**CI exception:** Merged through the guarded, explicitly [owner-approved exception](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/135528#issuecomment-5552148060) for run 33967056690, attempt 1. All 134 successful jobs and five intentional skips are retained; the only failed child jobs were:

- [Android tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33967056690/job/101309008344): reconnect acknowledgement times out in a scripted-Gateway fixture; progress-card markup fails because the expand control is absent before its markup assertions. These use Android's separate schema-1 Room store and local screenshot responses, not the changed Workshop/Gateway implementation. Android source and build inputs are unchanged against the actual CI merge base.
- [UI end-to-end test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33967056690/job/101309008116): the unchanged sidebar menu test times out after expand because the session link intercepts the button click (`session-management.sidebar.e2e.test.ts:236,298`). The complete UI, styles, test configuration and dependency lockfile are unchanged; the scenario uses a mocked Gateway and does not execute Workshop.

No unrelated CI code was changed. No introducing commit or matching-main failure is claimed for these test failures; this uses the explicit owner-approval route, not the automated matching-main exception.

Production net: +1,390 lines. Tests/support net: +5,262 lines. The growth provides the agent ownership boundary and migration/recovery proof; obsolete ownership and duplicate write paths were removed. Both PRs were unstacked; #136110 remains open and was not included in this landing.
